title: Canonicalize cached-response personalization metering and billing attribution
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: We observe inconsistencies between the inference-side token accounting and the billing ledger when cached responses are returned and then lightly personalized server-side (name insertion, suffixes, tracking tokens). In some cases the cache hit path reports zero generation tokens but downstream personalization or delivery components introduce additional token-like content which is either double-counted or not attributed correctly. This leads to surprise line items for customers and incorrect per-tenant chargebacks.

Goal: Define and implement a canonical event model and telemetry contract that cleanly separates: 1) model generation tokens (billable compute), 2) cache-hit metadata (no generation cost), and 3) personalization/post-processing adjustments (only bill if model compute consumed). Ensure streaming and partial-response flows (e.g., incremental preview + final personalization) do not cause double-billing. Provide migration and audit tooling to reclassify recent invoices where applicable.

Scope: server-side cache layer, personalization middleware (post-processors), billing event producer, metering pipeline normalization, e2e tests and dashboards. Not in scope: client-side SDKs (except where they emit metadata that affects server reconciliation).
acceptance_criteria: Define canonical event types and attributes and publish telemetry contract: event_type in {GENERATION, CACHE_HIT, PERSONALIZATION}, tokens:int, source_component:string, trace_id present
Billing pipeline consumes canonical events and charges only on GENERATION tokens; cache hits are zero-generation and do not generate token charges
PERSONALIZATION events are annotated with origin (server_transform|attachment_merge) and do not trigger generation billing unless they caused a model call
Streaming case: when personalization is applied mid-stream (patch/append) the pipeline must dedupe and ensure final billed token total equals the model-generated tokens only
Add unit tests for the canonicalizer, integration tests that simulate cache-hit + personalization + retry scenarios, and one end-to-end replay test that runs against a shadow billing store
Create a migration job that reprocesses the last 30 days to reclassify ambiguous records and produce reconciliation reports for Finance
Dashboard and alerting: card showing daily reclassified_events_count, top tenants impacted, and expected revenue delta; alert if reclassified events > 0.1% of daily events
comments: 2025-11-05 Maya Patel: Initial triage. Repro steps attached in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Cache+Personalization+Metering. Observed symptoms: cache hit path reported generation_tokens=0 but downstream delivery reported tokenized_length>0; unclear which component is authoritative.

2025-11-07 Liam Chen: Spike complete. Added a shim to the edge proxy that emits 'cache_hit' and a token_breakdown header. Found a race where the personalization layer appends a suffix inside the same streaming connection, which caused both the cache and personalization to emit token counts leading to double-counting in aggregator. Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/11234

2025-11-10 Priya Rao (PM): Decided canonical event model needed. Proposed attributes: event_type, tokens, token_source, personalization_kind, provenance_trace. PM doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-cache-personalization-metering

2025-11-12 Design review (Noah Kim): UX for console billing page to surface cache-hit vs generated cost approved. Will add an explanatory hover copy and sample invoice excerpt. Design spec: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/CachePersonalizationBilling

2025-11-14 Eng sync: Implementation plan accepted. Steps: (1) telemetry contract, (2) aggregator canonicalizer, (3) billing pipeline filter update, (4) migration/reprocess job, (5) dashboards & alerts. Blocking: need a replay queue with higher retention to run migration without impacting production throughput.

2025-11-18 Liam Chen: Migration job prototype pushed to branch cache-metering-migration. Performance note: reprocessing 7 days of raw events estimated at 6 hours on current infra; will request INF quota for a 30-day backfill. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/220
notes: Edge cases to watch: 1) clients that add client-side previews then confirm causing two separate requests (should be treated as exploratory and only final confirmed request billed per product policy), 2) attachments merged post-generation that increase payload length but are not model tokens, 3) retry paths where cached response is invalidated mid-flight and triggers model call
Finance asked for a conservative migration first: tag suspect invoices and provide a report before auto-crediting customers
Consider adding a small fixed service fee for heavy personalization transforms if they materially increase delivery costs (separate product discussion required)
